title: Opportunistic mini-batcher and adaptive quant prober
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: large-production customers see intermittent cost spikes when request size distribution shifts; current batching heuristics are conservative and quantization profiles are static for rollout windows. Motivation: reduce steady-state token cost for bursty tail workloads while preserving latency SLO and avoiding regressions caused by aggressive quantization. What this PR does: introduces an "opportunistic mini-batcher" scheduling path that inserts short horizon micro-batches for small, latency-tolerant requests and collapses them into regular batches when throughput increases; adds an adaptive quant prober that runs low-risk probe requests (shadow-mode) to measure output fidelity and latency/throughput tradeoffs across candidate quant profiles; surfaces profile scorecards to the Optimize suggestions engine and Redwood Console. Safety and rollout: default is opt-in for Dedicated and Private customers via a config flag; system-level safeties include deterministic fallbacks to baseline model variants if probe drift or eval regressions exceed thresholds; can be disabled per-model. Backwards compatibility: API unchanged, purely behind a feature flag and config knobs. Checklist: [x] unit + integration tests, [x] perf benchmarks on p3/p4, [x] added console telemetry hooks, [x] docs/quickstart added. Related: ENG-1742 (batching heuristics rewrite), ENG-1780 (quant probe infra), SUP-433 (customer incident motivating work).

review_comments: Devon: Can you clarify how the mini-batcher interacts with the existing prefix cache? Potential for duplicate cache warmups.

Author(Maya): The mini-batcher attaches to the existing KV cache layer; it tags micro-batch requests so they reuse prefix entries and we skip redundant warms. Added tests to validate no extra cache churn.
Anika: Quant probes look promising. How are we ensuring probe inputs are representative and not leaking PII?
Author(Maya): Probes are sampled from anonymized synthetic replay or user-approved prompt sets. Default probes are synthetic; customer can opt-into live sampling with KMS and audit logging enabled.
Romain: CI flaked on one perf test initially; saw a timeout on p3. Re-run fixed it. Approving.
Devon: Recommend adding a fail-open mode in case probe scoring service is unavailable.
Author(Maya): Added fail-open behavior that gracefully disables suggestions but keeps batching on baseline settings; updated docs and tests.

release_notes: Introduce an opportunistic mini-batching scheduler that reduces unit token cost for small/latency-tolerant requests; add adaptive quant prober to safely probe quant profiles and feed recommendations into Redwood Optimize and Console; feature gated behind a config flag for Dedicated/Private deployments; includes telemetry and safety fallbacks.
notes_for_release: Default disabled for Hosted customers; operators can enable via 'batching.opportunistic.enabled' and configure 'quant.prober.sampling_rate' and 'probe.eval_threshold'. See docs/quickstarts/mini_batch_defaults.md for recommended presets per workload type.
qa_summary: Ran synthetic replay of 3 representative workloads (conversational, single-turn completion, embeddings) across p3/p4, measured median latency change (-3% to +1%), 95th percentile latency (+/- 2% with safe knobs), and token unit cost improvements (6-18%) depending on skew. All regression checks passed.
